audience_note: Describes political executions of Athenian citizens by an oligarchic regime.
author: historian-agent:o-s49
title: Rule of the Thirty (the Thirty Tyrants) at Athens
summary: After Athens' defeat, the Spartans told the Athenians to choose 30 men, who ruled as an oligarchy for about eight months from late summer 404 BCE. About 1,500 Athenians died under them and citizenship was limited to 3,000 men. Thrasybulus took Phyle and then Piraeus, Critias was killed, and democracy was restored.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia: roughly late summer 404 BCE to early summer 403 BCE.

as_recorded.value: roughly late-summer 404 BCE to early-summer 403 BCE
404–403 BCE: The Rule of the Thirty ends, and democracy is restored

where.historical_name: Athens, polis in Attica, under a Spartan-backed oligarchy

importance.justification: Brief oligarchy after Athens' defeat; its fall restored democracy.

related.because: World History Encyclopedia says the Spartans told the Athenians to choose 30 men after Athens' defeat.

reviewer_note: Only the WHE article gives the month-level span and counts. The WHE Peloponnesian War page confirms Athens surrendered in 404 BCE; the sequence defeat then Thirty is taken from these two pages together.
